svg.text: The console on an ESP32: the chip, the screen and the knob on two breadboards
21 jumper wires, and 6 more for the optional buttons (dashed). Plug them in number order with the USB cable unplugged. Red = 3.3 V, black = ground.
Freenove's ESP32-WROVER (40 pins), camera unplugged, from the top, USB-C to the left. It bridges two breadboards, its pins in row j of the top board
and row a of the bottom one, each pin with 4 free holes beside it on the outside (f-i above, b-e below). Wire by the names printed next to the pins.
CLK = A, DT = B, SW = SW1,
+ and GND to the top rails
its 8 pins in the order printed on it, BL to GND
(header on the right, top to bottom)
SCL here is the screen's clock,
a dot = the end goes in that hole
Before the USB cable goes in
- Nothing in the 5V holes (left pins 19 and 20, next to the USB end): it is 5 V and the screen and the chip want 3.3 V.
- The camera is unplugged: its ribbon shares IO4, IO5, IO18, IO19, IO21, IO22, IO23, IO25, IO26 and IO27 with the screen, chip and knob.
- The top red rail has wires 1 and 3 (and a KY-040's +); the bottom red rail has 3, 5 and 15. No red wire in a blue rail, no black in a red one.
- A meter on continuity from a red rail to a blue rail must not beep.
